clue.text: Hear whether having meals is protection from rain

indicators.note: Hear tells the solver to take the next word by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: the conjunction whether is pronounced the same as the word for the climate
boarding is the provision of meals, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: Someone wonders about the weather while eating, and whether a meal counts as shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' turns WHETHER into its sound-alike WEATHER; 'having' joins it to BOARDING.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlapping horizontal planks fixed to an outside wall shed water and shield the building from the weather.

clue.text: Seems to pose the question of a strange woman

indicators.note: Seems to here means sounds like, so the question-word is taken by its pronunciation

parts.note: asking which? is posing the question of choice

explanation.surface: Someone is puzzled about a peculiar woman and asks who she is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seems to' is the sound signal: the questioning word WHICH is said the same as WITCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorceress is the classic odd, uncanny woman of folklore.

clue.text: Changing to Saturn, a heavenly voyager

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: Changing says the letters of to, Saturn and a are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spacefarer alters course for the ringed planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing' rearranges TO and SATURN into STRONAUT; the A printed last in the clue goes at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A space traveller journeys among the heavens, the bodies of the sky.

clue.text: Suspend dynasty with gravity

parts.note: the Han were a ruling dynasty of ancient China
g is the physics symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: A royal house is put on hold with great solemnity.
explanation.definitionFit: To dangle something from a hook or rope is to keep it held up in the air.

clue.text: Bend back and bring back to a better state about five

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one piece is placed round the other

parts.words: bring back to a better state
parts.note: recure is an old verb meaning to restore or heal
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A therapist advises bending over backwards and restoring health within five sessions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts RECURE around V; RECURE is an archaic word for restoring to health.
explanation.definitionFit: A curve turned backwards on itself, as on an archer's bow, is a recurve.

clue.text: Projection in a building fired

explanation.surface: A part of a building juts out after being shot at.
explanation.walkthrough: An outshot is a lean-to or projecting extension; read as two words, out-shot is something discharged outwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An extension built out from the main wall juts out from it; and anything fired has been shot out.

clue.text: Sway and spring, hemmed in by rock

parts.note: to sway back and forth is to rock
a spring or leap is a bound

explanation.surface: A climber sways and leaps while trapped among cliffs.
explanation.definitionFit: Bound used as a suffix means confined, so this describes a place enclosed by stone.

clue.text: I make a point about one being a fool

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to dot is to mark with a point
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A speaker insists on stating a point about someone being foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts DOT around I (one), after the opening I.
explanation.definitionFit: A simpleton or dunce is a stupid person.

clue.text: Producer of the information age, on a mountain

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
an era is an age
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor in England

explanation.surface: A source of the information age sits atop a peak.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is informal British for information; a TOR is a craggy hilltop in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo or power plant makes electricity, so it is a maker of energy.

clue.text: Ship I beat in less than a moment

indicators.note: in places the first pair inside the shortened word
less than means falling short, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a tick is a moment, as in just a tick
to tan someone's hide is to beat them

explanation.surface: A vessel is thrashed in no time at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface implies a ship is beaten; 'beat' actually supplies letters, and the moment is trimmed by 'less than'.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous liner that struck an iceberg in 1912 was a vessel.

clue.text: Contact in time and deed

parts.note: a deed is an action

explanation.surface: Someone makes contact at the right moment with a deed.
explanation.definitionFit: Taction is a rare word for touching, the act of physical contact.

clue.text: Ring for dancing without love

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A ring dance goes on with no romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: HOP goes round O.
explanation.definitionFit: A circular band, as in a hoop earring or a child's hoop, is a ring shape.

clue.text: Forbidder for hospital with one eater

parts.note: pro means in favour of, so for
H is the map abbreviation for hospital
I is the Roman numeral for one
a biter is one who bites, an eater

explanation.surface: Someone bans a hospital patient who eats too much.
explanation.definitionFit: One who bans something forbids it.

clue.text: Bachelor swallowed by a single shell-fish

indicators.note: swallowed by says the first piece is enclosed by the following words

parts.note: single means alone
B is the abbreviation for Bachelor, as in a degree

explanation.surface: An unmarried man is eaten by a lone mollusc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowed by' puts B inside A + ALONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The ormer or sea-ear is an edible mollusc with an iridescent shell.

clue.text: Mainly a policeman with detectives rising — necessarily true

annotationWithheld.why: Mainly a policeman with detectives rising — necessarily true (9): no parse found for APODICTIC; detectives reversed gives DIC but 'Mainly a policeman' cannot be made to supply APO and TIC around it, and no blog or database gives the wordplay
annotationWithheld.clue: Mainly a policeman with detectives rising — necessarily true

clue.text: Disguise the roving during darkness

indicators.note: Disguise as a command says alter the look of the letters, rearranging them

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wandering conceals themselves at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disguise' rearranges THE and ROVING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done through the night happens while it is dark.

clue.text: Holiday-maker goes to ancient city and is in Germany

parts.note: Ur was a city of ancient Mesopotamia
ist is German for is

explanation.surface: A traveller heads to a ruin and then into Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in Germany' means the German word for 'is', IST; UR is the biblical city of Abraham.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on vacation visiting places is a sightseer.

clue.text: Defective cognition is unknown

indicators.note: Defective says the word cognition is faulty and its letters must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Faulty thinking leaves one unaware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defective' rearranges COGNITION.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling under a false name means not being recognised.

clue.text: Dismissed permits for selling places

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
lets means allows or permits

explanation.surface: Someone sacked is allowed to run the shops.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops and stores where goods are sold are retail points.

clue.text: Treason with a politician going wrong

indicators.note: going wrong says the letters of treason go astray into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Treachery involving a corrupt legislator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going wrong' rearranges TREASON.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a senate is an elected lawmaker.

clue.text: Vehicle went fast and is back

indicators.note: back says the combined letters are read from right to left

parts.note: raced means went fast
taken as written

explanation.surface: A car sped off and has now returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the whole run, so the vehicle's name comes out from the end of 'went fast' and 'is' read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-wheeled passenger car attached to a motorcycle is a vehicle.

clue.text: Dexterity sounds trifling

indicators.note: sounds says the next word is to be heard, not read

parts.note: slight means trifling or minor

explanation.surface: Skill with the hands is said to be a minor thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds' makes SLIGHT give its sound-alike SLEIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight of hand is nimble manual skill.

clue.text: Threats from one mile pit north of these in France

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a pit is a mine
ces is French for these

explanation.surface: Dangers lie a mile from a mine north of these French places.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer 'north of' simply means 'before'; the French word for 'these' ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Things about to happen, especially dangers, loom as menaces.

clue.text: Animal which shows there may be some ado about nothing

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled letters go round the piece for nothing
ado is fuss or bother, so the letters of some are stirred up

parts.note: nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A creature shows that there may be a little fuss over nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ado' is the anagram signal on SOME, making MOSE, and 'about' puts it round O.
explanation.definitionFit: The elk of North America is a large deer.

clue.text: Made do without a man when old

indicators.note: without means lacking, so letters are removed

parts.note: to make do is to manage
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone coped alone without a partner in later life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes MAN from MANAGED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone advanced in years is elderly.

clue.text: Copes without start of grace for chief magistrates

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means one piece encloses the other

parts.note: one who copes gets by, or does, as in she does well enough

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of grace

explanation.surface: A man copes without graceful beginnings in high office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside: DOES goes round G, the first letter picked by 'start of' grace.
explanation.definitionFit: The doge was the elected head of state of Venice or Genoa, its leading magistrate.

clue.text: Fish's heart of the people

indicators.note: heart means only the central part is kept, the first and last letters going

parts.note: plaice is a European flatfish

explanation.surface: A fish's heart belongs to the people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' strips the first and last letters from PLAICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Laic means lay, belonging to ordinary people rather than clergy.

clue.text: Thinking even if it is time

parts.note: though means even if

explanation.surface: Reflecting on whether the moment has come.
explanation.definitionFit: The process of reasoning in the mind is thought.

clue.text: Wearing away the bars

explanation.surface: Something erodes the metal rods.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is rasping or abrading; the other is the framework of bars over a drain or window.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbing against a rough surface abrades it; and a grid of parallel metal rods is a grille.

clue.text: The cross is broken outside to defend and cover

indicators.note: outside says the rearranged letters surround the next piece
is broken says the letters of the cross are smashed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
to defend is to protect

explanation.surface: A broken crucifix stands outside a church to guard and shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is broken' rearranges THE CROSS to make CHEST ORS, split round the middle piece by 'outside'; such guards are worn by catchers or wicketkeepers.
explanation.definitionFit: Padded guards worn over the torso by baseball catchers or cricketers shield the body.
